newsitem.title: USA: Houston again postpones water bond refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Houston again postpones water bond refinancing.

text.p: Unfavorable market conditions on Monday again stopped the City of Houston from refinancing up to $450 million of water and sewer revenue bonds, city officials said.
John Baldwin, deputy finance director for the city's public works department, said he does not expect conditions to improve for the rest of this week.

"The markets are not favorable today and chances are they won't happen this week," Baldwin told Reuters. "So our deal is not there today. We will keep trying every day, but we won't do it until we are sure."
The bonds currently carry average interest rates of about six percent, but the city wants to bring them below 5.4 percent, producing present value savings of between $12 million and $16 million.
Baldwin said a refunding in Monday's market would only bring savings of about $8 million to $10 million "and the maximum we would have done is about $250 million out of about $450 million."
The refinancing, which the city had hoped to complete last week, will be handled by a team of nine underwriters led by Merrill Lynch & Co.
Houston's water and sewer department currently has a bonded debt of about $2.5 billion.
